title: How to say it: one song's words, written to be said
description: The format in say/<song-id>.json, for a song not in English. The app's "How to say it" panel shows it only when `reviewed` is true and every line has its recording: a real person saying the line slowly, never synth speech. tools/say_check.py checks the rest: the song exists and its language is this one, every word the parts sing is in a line, no line says a word the song doesn't sing, and a Jewish song writes no full divine name.

song.description: The song's id, as the file is named.

style.description: Latin only: church (Italianate, as choirs sing it) or classical.

reviewed.description: False until a native speaker or a voice teacher has checked every word's sounds. Shown only when true.

reviewer.description: Who checked it, as a role, never a name. Needed when reviewed.

lines.description: Each line of words once, in the order the song first sings them; a repeat isn't written again.

words.description: The line as the song writes it, without its syllable dashes.

sounds.description: Each word of the line, in order, and how it's said.

say.description: Plain sounds an English reader says without a key: syllables joined by hyphens, the stressed one in capitals ("sah-krah-MEN-toom"). No phonetic symbols.

clip.description: The spoken recording's id, <song>/<nn>; null until a real person has recorded it.
